Definition: from G303 and G2896; to scream up (aloud):--cry out.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to cry out, to scream aloud: a man with an unclean spirit in the synagogue cried out when Jesus came near, and the crowd before Pilate cried out all at once, 'Away with this man, and release unto us Barabbas.' It is a shout, not a conversation — the cry of a spirit being driven out, and the cry of a crowd demanding a death.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for crying out carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two shouts — a demon crying out before Jesus, and a crowd crying out for Barabbas.
